persons.name: Berk Dinçtürk
persons.digest:
In both broadcasts Berk Dinçtürk repeats his core thesis: whoever wins the US election, the US will keep pulling production back home and pursuing its critical-mineral and technology strategy, so **AI** spending and its hardware side (semiconductors, memory, energy, nuclear) keep standing out. He calls the bubble talk a distortion by headlines; he explains that the Broadcom CEO's remark reads differently in full and points to memory stocks such as **Micron**. In cybersecurity he likes **PANW** and **CRWD** but is not buying today because he expects an index correction in 2027, after which this is the first group he would buy.

On macro he says the Fed will skip at this meeting and the bar for cutting is far lower than the bar for hiking; for **Brent** he sees no problem with oil flows and expects a quick drop on normalization. He says he closed his Brazil ETF over second-round risk but the theme is not over. He says **Bitcoin** has a clear road ahead, **Ethereum** and **Solana** may benefit from tokenization, the **gold** and **silver** story has not changed, and that by the end of Trump's term silver could be three digits and gold five digits. If Japan hikes rates, he expects a decline in **GBP/JPY** over the next two months.

items.title: I Think Bitcoin Has a Clear Road Ahead in the Coming Years! 🪙💵₿
items.summary: Berk Dinçtürk says that whoever wins the election, the US strategy of reshoring production and securing critical minerals and technology will not change; a Democratic win would suit markets more but could bring AI regulation and a rotation into healthcare. On oil he says flows are fine, the price carries a risk premium, the ideal Brent band for the US industrial shift is $75-85, and easing Russian sanctions and indirect Iranian supply could push it lower. He argues the Fed will skip at this meeting, the US cannot push its economy into recession with $40 trillion of debt, and the bar for cuts is much lower than for hikes. He is weak on Europe because of energy costs, bureaucracy and French bond yields, and thinks the problem will spread to Italy. On Brazil he notes CDS rose from 119 to 151 bp after Lula's win, says he closed his position last week over second-round risk, but the theme is not over. In cybersecurity he names Palo Alto and CrowdStrike as the first group he would buy after a 2027 correction. He says Bitcoin has a clear road ahead, the crypto market could multiply 3-5x from $4 trillion, and Ethereum and Solana may also benefit from tokenization. He notes gold fell from $5,000 to $4,000 but the uptrend is not over, and predicts silver at three digits and gold at five digits by the end of Trump's term. He likes healthcare, semiconductors and memory (Micron), nuclear/SMR and copper, and says he is done with the Russell. He adds that a Japanese rate hike could shake carry trades and that he expects GBP/JPY to fall within two months.

items.title: Is AI a Bubble? - Berk Dinçtürk
items.summary: Berk Dinçtürk says that for three years every three months someone has declared the AI bubble is bursting, and the latest case was a Broadcom CEO remark twisted in a headline. He says that in the full text the CEO said those who do not understand why $50 billion was reported when $70 billion of profit was expected from OpenAI do not know the accounting standard, and that the 'gambling' line was cherry-picked from it. He argues AI spending is $700 billion this year, $1.3 trillion next year and $10 trillion by 2032, and that calling a bubble with traditional gauges such as the Buffett indicator only breeds fear. With the shift from software to hardware he expects semiconductors, memory, energy, uranium, rare earths, copper and silver to stay in demand. He notes the US, Russia and China have declared these materials strategic reserves.

assets.note: Explains that the Broadcom CEO's 'gambling' remark was cherry-picked in the headline and the full text differs.
Says silver will keep seeing demand from AI and strategic-reserve buying.
Says copper will keep seeing demand from AI and strategic-reserve buying.
